archives: Both archive convictions retained without re-judgement. Only the requested stranded members are assigned new markers.
verdict_basis: These members are executable webshell or bind/reverse-shell payloads. Their direct request-to-command or network-to-shell I/O paths tip the artifact verdict to MALICIOUS. Project banners, scanner scores and the containing archives do not establish these behaviors. The packaging as penetration-testing templates is legitimate dual-use provenance; it does not make these standalone access payloads ordinary documentation or utility libraries.
missing_context: No evidence establishes deployment to a web server, successful execution, authorized testing, a compromised host, an operator identity or an active public callback. Unpatched private/placeholder addresses and the PHP syntax defect limit immediate operability; the payload code and intended control paths are still present.

relocations.severity: baseline to notable: identifies a CPU architecture
baseline to notable: identifies a CPU architecture

intentional_detection_changes: PHP reverse-shell inference now requires a bound proc_open shell launch instead of an unrelated interactive-shell literal.
Pentestmonkey payload identity becomes hostile only when both its banner and the independently established reverse-shell relay match. Banner-only identity stays notable.
S/390 architecture properties become notable, and SPARC V9 gets a distinct machine-field observation. Two-byte header matches are pinned at ELF e_machine.
An encoded Runtime.exec member reference moves to source-member syntax; its execution ATT&CK mapping is removed.
The native exec-family exclusion reuses the existing node-pty basename fact (its existing 500 MB size ceiling applies).

The Netcat consumer no longer requires an unrelated generic spawn finding in addition to its mandatory -e/--exec shell evidence. The required endpoint and shell-command evidence must be within 1024 bytes.
ancestor_audit: Loader-variable facts remain under micro-behaviors/os; no os/linker directory selectors select the moved leaf.
Executable references remain under fs/path/application; basename-only observations move to fs/path/basename. Exact consumers and active fixture destinations are updated.
Native exec-family moves within process/create. Its old execv directory selector is Python-only and cannot select native-only ELF/Mach-O evidence.
The sole shell/spawn directory consumer was the Netcat composite; its redundant spawn condition is corrected and has direct-shell, listener and no-shell controls.
The mainframe architecture selector contained only the two S/390 rules and is replaced with the S/390 selector, preserving its member set.
Existing runtime/exec directory consumers intentionally cease treating a decoded member reference as process-execution evidence; their other launch requirements remain.

members.marker_note: Laudanum PHP shell: command backdoor with a PHP syntax defect
members.behavior: After the IP allowlist, session/nonce/password authentication gates POST command execution through proc_open and output pipes. A missing semicolon after the users array prevents this exact file from parsing; legacy curly-brace indexing also requires an older PHP version. The bytes are a broken command-webshell payload, not inert documentation.

members.marker_note: Laudanum ASP shell: IP-gated requests execute arbitrary commands
members.behavior: REMOTE_ADDR is compared with a configured address and rejected clients receive a 404. Submitted cmd data flows through WScript.Shell.Exec and StdOut.ReadAll into the HTTP response. No shell is assumed until a supplied command explicitly invokes one.

members.marker_note: Laudanum WP shell: POST commands run with authentication disabled
members.behavior: Includes ipcheck.php, then copies POST command input. The execution block is unconditional if(true), while the login UI is disabled with if(false). proc_open executes the selected command and stdout/stderr are rendered in a terminal form. The IP include is a dependency, not proof of successful access control when this member is deployed alone.

members.marker_note: Laudanum WAR: HTTP parameter directly executes OS commands
members.behavior: WAR contains an inert manifest and servlet descriptor plus cmd.jsp. The JSP passes request.getParameter("cmd") directly into Runtime.getRuntime().exec and returns process output. No authentication is implemented in the page; no shell interpreter is forced by Runtime.exec itself.

members.marker_note: WP PHP reverse shell: POST-selected socket relays shell I/O; rules fixed
members.behavior: POST ip/port values (with private-address defaults) select an outbound fsockopen connection. proc_open receives uname/w/id plus /bin/sh -i. Nonblocking stream_select and fread/fwrite relay peer bytes to child stdin and child stdout/stderr back to the same peer. Optional fork/setsid detaches the process.

members.marker_note: Pentestmonkey PHP: socket relays /bin/sh I/O; rules fixed
members.behavior: A configured private address and port select an outbound fsockopen connection. proc_open starts uname/w/id plus /bin/sh -i. Readiness-driven reads and writes connect the peer to child stdin/stdout/stderr. Optional fork/setsid, chdir and umask are setup operations; no file-persistence mechanism was observed.

members.marker_note: Laudanum hidden PHP: request variables select function and argument
members.behavior: extract($_REQUEST) imports request-controlled variable names in overwrite mode. The next executable statement invokes the variable callable with a variable argument inside die(). This provides arbitrary PHP-function dispatch, including OS-command functions. The @ operators suppress diagnostics; there is no encoded payload to decode and no IP or credential gate.

members.marker_note: GoAhead bind aarch64: load-time listener gives shell; paths fixed
members.behavior: Gzip expands to a stripped Linux ELF shared library. Its initialization-array entry clears LD_PRELOAD and forks; the parent exits. The child creates a TCP socket, enables address reuse, binds all interfaces on placeholder port 55555, listens and accepts a client; it closes the listening socket and duplicates the accepted descriptor onto descriptors 0, 1 and 2. It loops over a table of shell executable paths using execl(path, "sh", NULL); failed execs try the next path. The shared object is an exploit payload template, not a normal networking library. The constructor and same-descriptor I/O paths were disassembled independently for this build.

native_evidence.notes: Static constructor and child socket-to-stdio execution paths reviewed; never loaded.
